transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I just feel completely worn out all the time. It doesn't really seem to matter if I get a full night in bed, I still wake up and my body just feels like it's made of sandbags. Just getting through a normal workday, or even doing something basic at home like folding the laundry... it takes absolutely everything I have right now.
Have you been feeling sad or hopeless lately?

Yeah, I have. Most days, actually. I wake up with this heavy, flat feeling right in my chest. I'll just sit at the kitchen table staring out at the yard, and... I don't know, I just feel like there's no good version of the future coming. So, yes, definitely hopeless.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in activities that you usually enjoy?

Yes, I really have. I used to make time for a lot of things—hiking, yoga, working in my garden... I also usually enjoy taking bird photos. But lately, I just keep canceling plans. I just let my camera sit in the closet because... well, none of it really feels worth the effort right now.
How long have you been feeling this way?

I'd say this depressed feeling... and just being so slowed down and exhausted all the time... it's been going on for about the past two months. Yeah, most days for the last couple of months, it's been exactly like this.
Before these past two months, have you ever had another period of at least two weeks when you felt similarly depressed and lost interest in things?
No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had bad days here and there, like anyone, but nothing that lasted for weeks like this. This is the first time I've felt this down for this long.
Did anything particularly stressful or upsetting happen shortly before these symptoms began?

Well, we did just take on a mortgage about two months ago. I guess right around then is when my mood kind of shifted. Before that, I was in this really overcharged state, pushing hard at work to make sure we could afford it. But since we actually signed the papers and got the mortgage, it's just been this low stretch.
During the day, do you actually fall asleep unintentionally, such as while working, talking, or sitting quietly?

No, I don't actually fall asleep during the day. I mean, I feel completely exhausted and dragged down, but I'm not nodding off while I'm at my desk or anything like that. I just feel tired all the time.
Have you been having trouble concentrating or making decisions lately?

Yes, very much so. At work, I'll... I can read the same survey results or a client email three times and still not really absorb any of it. It just doesn't sink in. And decisions are just as bad. Even something small, like choosing which spreadsheet to open first, can feel weirdly impossible right now.
When you are not thinking about the mortgage or finances, do you still feel depressed most of the time?

Yeah, I do. It's not just the finances. Most days I wake up with this heavy, flat feeling right in my chest. I can just sit at the kitchen table staring out at the yard, and... I don't know, I just feel like there is no good version of the future coming. It's just there, whether I'm thinking about the mortgage or not.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a first depressive episode lasting approximately two months with depressed mood, anhedonia, marked fatigue, impaired concentration and decision-making, and hopelessness occurring most days, with clear occupational and daily-life impairment. The symptom burden supports a moderate major depressive episode. Adjustment disorder was considered because symptoms began around a mortgage-related stressor, but the depressive syndrome is sufficiently pervasive and meets criteria for a major depressive episode. Bipolar II disorder was considered due to a preceding description of feeling 'overcharged,' but no clear hypomanic episode was established. Persistent depressive disorder is unlikely because the duration is less than two years.
